p_panel.title: Look at the printer itself
p_panel.text: Is it switched on and awake? Press a button to wake it from sleep. Check the display or warning lights for a paper jam, an open cover, an empty tray or a cartridge or toner message. Windows often reports a printer with an error simply as 'Offline'.

p_usb.title: Try another USB port and cable
p_usb.text: Plug the cable straight into a USB port on the PC – not into a hub, dock or keyboard. Try a different port, and a different cable if you have one. Windows usually reports 'Device connected' or installs the printer again within a minute.

p_netstatus.title: Check the printer's network status
p_netstatus.text: On the printer's control panel, open the Wi-Fi or network menu – or print a network configuration report (often under Settings, Reports, or by holding the Wi-Fi or information button; the manual has the exact way). Note the network name (SSID) and the IP address. The network name must match the one your PC uses.

p_othertest.title: Print from a phone or another computer
p_othertest.text: On an iPhone or iPad, open a photo or web page and use Share > Print (AirPrint). On Android, use the share menu or the app's menu > Print. If the phone prints, the printer and the network work and the problem is on the PC.

p_restart.title: Restart in order: printer off, router, printer on, PC
p_restart.text: Switch the printer off. Restart the router and wait until the internet works again. Switch the printer on and give it a minute to rejoin the Wi-Fi. Finally restart the PC. The order matters: the printer should rejoin a router that is already up.

p_queue.title: Open the print queue and cancel stuck jobs
p_queue.text: Cancel every document in the list – one stuck job blocks everything after it. If the queue window has a 'Printer' menu, make sure 'Use Printer Offline' and 'Pause Printing' are not ticked; if there is no Printer menu in the queue window, skip that part. On some versions the classic queue is also reachable through Control Panel > Devices and Printers > right-click the printer > See what's printing.

paths.win11: Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners > (your printer) > Open print queue
paths.win10: Settings > Devices > Printers & scanners > (your printer) > Open queue

p_copy.title: Check for a second copy of the printer
p_copy.text: When a printer gets a new network address, Windows sometimes adds it again – for example as 'Printer name (Copy 1)'. The old entry stays offline while the copy works. Print to the entry that says Idle or Ready and make it the default. If Windows keeps switching your default printer, turn off 'Let Windows manage my default printer'.

paths.win11: Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners > Let Windows manage my default printer
paths.win10: Settings > Devices > Printers & scanners > Let Windows manage my default printer

p_copy.undo: Switch 'Let Windows manage my default printer' back on, or set the other printer as default again.

p_spooler.title: Restart the Print Spooler service
p_spooler.text: The Print Spooler is the Windows service that hands documents to printers. Restarting it clears a queue that refuses to empty. In the Services window, right-click Print Spooler > Restart – or use the command below in a Command Prompt opened with 'Run as administrator'.

paths.win11: Start > type Services > open Services > Print Spooler > right-click > Restart
paths.win10: Start > type Services > open Services > Print Spooler > right-click > Restart

cmds.code: net stop spooler && net start spooler
cmds.what: Stops the print service and starts it again. Documents still waiting in the queue may be lost.
cmds.not: It does not remove printers or drivers and changes no settings.

p_rejoin.title: Reconnect the printer to your Wi-Fi
p_rejoin.text: Use the Wi-Fi setup on the printer's control panel (often called Wireless Setup Wizard) or the printer maker's official app. Choose the same network the PC uses. Many home printers only work on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi; if your router uses one name for 2.4 and 5 GHz this usually works automatically.
p_rejoin.undo: Run the same Wi-Fi setup again and choose the previous network.

p_reserve.title: Give the printer a fixed address in the router
p_reserve.text: If the printer keeps going offline after router restarts, its IP address probably changes. In the router's app or admin page, look for DHCP reservation, address reservation or 'always use this IP address' and reserve the printer's current address.
p_reserve.undo: Delete the reservation in the same router menu.

p_readd.title: Remove the printer and add it again
p_readd.text: Removing and adding the printer makes Windows find it at its current address and reinstall its connection. If Windows doesn't list it, choose the option to add it manually and enter its IP address from the network report.

paths.win11: Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners > (your printer) > Remove, then Add device
paths.win10: Settings > Devices > Printers & scanners > (your printer) > Remove device, then Add a printer or scanner

p_readd.undo: Add the printer again with 'Add device' (Windows 11) or 'Add a printer or scanner' (Windows 10).

p_driver.title: Install the driver from the printer maker's own website
p_driver.text: Type the manufacturer's address yourself (for example the support site of HP, Canon, Epson or Brother) and pick your exact model. Don't use search ads, 'driver download' portals or driver updater tools – fake printer-support sites are a known scam pattern.
p_driver.undo: Uninstall the printer software again under Settings > Apps > Installed apps (Windows 11) or Settings > Apps (Windows 10).

q_printer.q: Is the printer on, awake and free of errors on its display?

answers.label: No – it shows an error or won't wake up

q_conn.q: How is the printer connected to this PC?

q_usb.q: After switching to another USB port (and cable), is the printer ready?

q_net.q: Is the printer connected to the same network as the PC?

answers.label: Yes, same network name, and it has an IP address
No – other network, or not connected

q_other.q: Can a phone or another computer print to it?

q_restart.q: Restart printer, router and PC in order. Is the printer online now?

q_queue.q: With the queue empty and 'Use Printer Offline' off, does the printer show as ready?

q_spooler.q: After restarting the Print Spooler, does it print?

r_printer.title: Likely here: the printer itself
r_printer.text: Windows can only report what the printer tells it. Clear the error shown on the printer first – paper, cover, cartridges – then switch it off and on. If the display shows an error code, look it up in the manual or on the maker's support site for your model.
r_printer.why: The printer reports a problem before any computer is involved.

r_usb.title: Solved: the USB connection
r_usb.text: A loose plug, a tired cable or an unpowered hub was interrupting the connection. Keep the printer on a port directly on the PC.
r_usb.why: Only the cable path changed, and the printer came back.

r_printer_wifi.title: Likely here: the printer is not on your Wi-Fi
r_printer_wifi.text: A printer on another network – or on none – is unreachable for the PC, which shows it as offline. This often happens after a new router, a changed Wi-Fi password or a power cut. Reconnect the printer, then reserve its address so it doesn't wander off again.
r_printer_wifi.why: The printer's own status shows a different network or no connection.

r_restart.title: Solved: the restart in the right order
r_restart.text: The printer had lost its place on the network – usually because the router gave it a new address or forgot it. If it happens again, give it a fixed address in the router.
r_restart.why: Nothing could print before, everything could after the ordered restart.

r_network.title: Likely here: printer and router aren't talking
r_network.text: No device can print, even after restarts. Reconnect the printer to the Wi-Fi from its own panel, check that it gets an IP address, and add it again on the PC. If the printer's network report shows no address, the printer's Wi-Fi setup or the router's settings are the problem – the maker's support site has model-specific steps.
r_network.why: Phones and the PC fail alike, so the shared part – printer and router – is left.

r_queue.title: Solved: a stuck queue or an offline setting
r_queue.text: Windows was waiting on a stuck document or had the printer set to offline use. Both live only on the PC – the printer and network were fine.
r_queue.why: Clearing the queue and its settings on the PC brought the printer back.

r_spooler.title: Solved: the Print Spooler had hung
r_spooler.text: The service that passes documents to printers had stopped responding. If this happens often, install the current driver from the printer maker's website.
r_spooler.why: Restarting only the spooler fixed it.

r_driver.title: Likely here: the printer's setup on this PC
r_driver.text: Other devices can print, so the printer and network work. On this PC the printer entry or its driver is stuck. Remove the printer and add it again; if that fails, install the driver package from the printer maker's own website.
r_driver.why: The fault survived the queue and spooler checks and only this PC is affected.
